Started playing aroung with mini.test because rolling my own testing ended up way more annoying than I thought. I found a small issue which is that in these situations, headless execution of `lua MiniTest.run()` and friends doesn't exit to the terminal, which could hang my CI:
- "No tests to execute." I guess this message is printed to the internal `v:errmsg`, because setting `collect = { silent = true }` in setup suppresses the message, but the nvim process still does not exit (which is even worse)
- syntax/Vim error in the `minimal_init.lua` (I think this gets picked up by the internal error buffer of the nvim process, bypassing mini.test completely, could be tricky to change)
- syntax/Vim error in a test file ("Sourcing <foo.lua> resulted in the following error: <errormsg>")

I tried setting `collect = { stop_on_error = true }` but that didn't help, as I suspect that option means "stop testing if we encounter ANY test failure", right?

It seems like some of this could be solved by adding some checks for `#vim.api.nvim_list_uis() == 0` which should trigger `vim.cmd.quit` or something like that.

  • syntax/Vim error in the minimal_init.lua (I think this gets picked up by the internal error buffer of the nvim process, bypassing mini.test completely, could be tricky to change)
  • syntax/Vim error in a test file ("Sourcing <foo.lua> resulted in the following error: ")

I tried setting collect = { stop_on_error = true } but that didn't help, as I suspect that option means "stop testing if we encounter ANY test failure", right?

It seems like some of this could be solved by adding some checks for #vim.api.nvim_list_uis() == 0 which should trigger vim.cmd.quit or something like that.

I have a realᵀᴹ example of this: Currently (Neovim 0.10) it is not possible to use `vim.cmd.silent(...)` with any kind of arguments. However, I have some API I want to test that may do `vim.print("foo")`. I need to catch/suppress the print output as it garbles test reporting. So I do `vim.cmd[[silent lua myfunc()]]`. Very good, but now I introduce an error in `myfunc` which I want my tests to report. They do so, but in headless mode my terminal remains blocked at that test (looks like some sort of nested `nvim_exec2` is going on).  If the error inside `myfunc` is somehow unique to the CI environment, it will cause the issue I am describing.

I can put this into a minimal reproducer if that helps, although I'm  also happy to accept that this is out of scope, in which case I'll think of some workarounds.

edit: `vim.cmd[[silent ...]]` was not the culprit, read [this](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/discussions/1079#discussioncomment-10128191)

reply_data.body: It sounds like an issue with hanging child process (see second bullet point  [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/TESTING.md#startstoprestart)). I don't think there is a way to actually remedy this because Neovim itself becomes blocked while it waits for user input. Sending non-blockingly something like `<Esc><Esc>` sometimes helps, but doing so in automated fashion introduces more problems than it solves (like, there is no good way of differentiating if the blocking is intentional or not, etc.).

edit: But for now, cleaning the `vim.t.myplugin` state in `post_case` solved it.

reply_data.body:
> ... tab-local state that **doesn't get cleared on `child.restart`** that was the cause ...

I am not sure how this is possible. `child.restart()` is quite literally [`stop()` and `start()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/657ef75b52a548090fb7906735517b7ddbf39e88/lua/mini/test.lua#L1148). And `stop()` [completely shuts the current process](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/657ef75b52a548090fb7906735517b7ddbf39e88/lua/mini/test.lua#L1128). So unless that same tabpage-local variable is defined after `child.start()` (like a side effect of 'minimal_init.lua' or some other executed code), it would be very strange to see it actually persist after restart.

reply_data.body:
I seem to be getting somewhere with this. Incidentally, using mini.nvim lead to this report: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/30051

I'm really enjoying the parametrised test capability in particular. I can even go crazy and pass function references as the parameters! And for the floating windows, using `uv.sleep(500)` seems to cover the worst cases (waiting for termopen).

Actually `vim.schedule` is not even required, I was just being silly before and didn't use `child` methods properly.

My `test/init.lua` (used by the setup hooks) now looks like this:

```
local command = vim.api.nvim_create_user_command
vim.opt.rtp:append(vim.fn.getcwd())

function TestInit()
    vim.opt.rtp:append('dep/mini.nvim')
    require('mini.test').setup({
        collect = {
            find_files = function()
                return vim.fn.globpath('test', '**/test_*.lua', true, true)
            end,
            -- silent = true,
        },
    })
    haunt = require('my_plugin')
    vim.cmd.helptags('ALL')
    my_plugin._err_blocking = true  -- Makes it use error() instead of vim.api.nvim_err_writeln so that expect.error and such work properly
end

command("TestInit", TestInit, { desc = "Initialise testing context" })
command("TestRun", [[=MiniTest.run()]], { desc = "Run test suite" })

-- Load test dependency automatically if headless.
if #vim.api.nvim_list_uis() == 0 then
    TestInit()
end
```

comment_data.body:
I agree that it would be bad practice to commit tests without running them locally, so it's not much of an issue. It just seemed like an incomplete UX to have headless mode not always automatically exit to terminal, but maybe that's just me. I could imagine a situation where CI is using a different neovim version than the local one (again, arguably PEBKAC) that introduced regressions and caused an error in a test file, preventing CI termination.

There are a few specific changes I made to the Makefile and `minimal_init.lua` immediately, which are not exactly related but since you asked I will list them:
- Declare `FILE =  $(error "specify the test file using a FILE=<name> assignment")` which will cause make to throw that error when attempting to read from an unset `FILE` variable for the `test_file` target (alternatively, using an `?=` assignment would allow for setting `FILE` as an env var instead of only inline in the make command)
- Use `deps/mini.nvim/.git` as the prerequisite for `test` and `test_file` targets, which will retain desired behaviour if `mini.test` is included as a git submodule instead of as a git clone
- In `minimal_init.lua`, factor the lines inside the `#vim.api.nvim_list_uis() == 0` check into a function so that setup for running tests from an interactive nvim session is as easy as calling that function

Can I also just confirm that `collect = { stop_on_error = true }` in the config does what I think it does, i.e.
> stop testing if we encounter ANY test failure

Nice tips, thanks!

> Can I also just confirm that `collect = { stop_on_error = true }` in the config does what I think it does, i.e.
> 
> > stop testing if we encounter ANY test failure

It should do what [is documented](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/657ef75b52a548090fb7906735517b7ddbf39e88/doc/mini-test.txt#L181-L182): if it is `true`, then after the first error (as a result of test case execution) the whole process (of executing test cases) stops. This is mostly to have allow less time if all you need to know is whether the whole suite passes or not.

title: [mini.test] Recommended setup for headless execution might not exit
